definitions.explanation: To get rid of something by putting it in the trash or otherwise disposing of it. To abandon or give up something.

examples.japanese: ゴミを{捨|す}ててください。
{古|ふる}い{服|ふく}を{捨|す}てました。
まだ{使|つか}えるから{捨|す}てないで。
examples.english: Don't throw it away because it's still usable.

examples.japanese: {壊|こわ}れた{傘|かさ}を{捨|す}てようと{思|おも}ったけど、まだ{直|なお}せるかもしれない。
examples.english: I was going to throw away the broken umbrella, but I might still be able to fix it.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{前|まえ}に、いらないものを{全部|ぜんぶ}{捨|す}てて、{新|あたら}しい{生活|せいかつ}を{始|はじ}めたいです。
examples.english: Before moving, I want to throw away everything I don't need and start a new life.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). No pair verb. Pattern: Xを{捨|す}てる (throw away X).

ASPECT: ている indicates completed action with result. {捨|す}てている = 'has thrown away' or 'is in the process of discarding.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・ゴミを{捨|す}てる (throw away trash)
・{古|ふる}いものを{捨|す}てる (throw away old things)
・{捨|す}てないで (don't throw it away)
・{夢|ゆめ}を{捨|す}てる (give up a dream - figurative)

Can mean 'to abandon' figuratively. Opposite: {拾|ひろ}う (to pick up).
